text: Right. Ok so im wondering if, and idk how much this could change things, but that final blob, could it itself be parted out per mesh, and technically allow for 'uploading' them in real time through the streaming as a side gain from it but also does ensure when i technically 'export' the game asset in the editor, it creates this file
resolution: Design answer, no code: confirmed the per-mesh parted blob IS the already-ruled architecture — V29 (content-addressed installable assets, mapfile installs assets then references by hash, GMod-dupe runtime install = the real-time upload path) and V31 (manifests over content-addressed chunk artifacts as streaming units). Mapped the missing piece: the editor's Export cooking a model package (authoring source) into an immutable hash-named binary asset artifact (raw f32 mesh + atlas + placeable/skeleton lumps) that installs into the asset store; the gamefile then references it instead of embedding. Laid out side gains (dedup, idempotent installs, per-asset streaming, incremental compile) and what building the cook step involves.
